name: embermeter
description: Embermeter: an animated live instrument panel for Claude Code, built for VS Code. Health grade, context composition and runway to auto-compact, token and cache analytics, cost burn and budget, rate-limit countdowns, particle flow diagram, tool leaderboard with p95, file heatmap, subagent swimlanes, permission gate, laptop vitals with a heat guard, and lifetime stats

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: washi: rice paper, sumi ink and a vermilion sun; night: warm ink instrument panel; day: plain paper; contrast: black ground and bright text for low vision and bright rooms. Each graphic paints its own ground, so any of them reads on any editor theme

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: smooth: eased transitions plus live particles and pulses (in the terminal, a spinner, pulses and a sweep while work runs); reduced: eased transitions only; off: static

openOnStart.title: Open on start
openOnStart.description: Open the Embermeter pane when a session starts

band.title: Strip above the prompt
band.description: Show the compact animated strip (grade, context, temp, battery, cost) above the prompt

terminalDrawing.title: Terminal drawing
terminalDrawing.description: graphics: coloured cell meters and charts in the CLI pane and strip; text: plain lines, for screen readers or terminals that draw block characters poorly

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: full: grade, state, context, cost, temperature, battery and agents; minimal: grade, state and context; cost: spend and burn rate; off: no status line

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Toast once when context, temperature, budget or a rate limit crosses its threshold

budgetUsd.title: Session budget (USD)
budgetUsd.description: Cost budget for one session; 0 turns the budget ring and alerts off

dailyBudgetUsd.title: Daily budget (USD)
dailyBudgetUsd.description: Cost budget for a calendar day across sessions; alerts at 80% and 100%. 0 turns it off

longTurnMin.title: Long turn (minutes)
longTurnMin.description: Alert when a single turn runs longer than this; 0 turns it off

turnBudgetUsd.title: Turn-cost stop (USD)
turnBudgetUsd.description: Refuse further tool calls once one turn has cost this much, so Claude stops and asks; 0 turns it off

loopBreak.title: Loop breaker
loopBreak.description: Refuse a third identical tool call in a row (same tool, same input), so Claude changes approach instead of looping

cacheAlert.title: Cache alert
cacheAlert.description: Toast a minute before the prompt cache goes cold after a reply, when the window holds 20k tokens or more; the countdown shows either way

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.description: Hours with no toasts, as start-end in 24h local time (for example 22-7); the panel keeps updating. Empty turns it off

guard.title: Heat guard
guard.description: Refuse heavy Bash jobs while the laptop is over the temperature limit or low on battery

maxTempC.title: Temperature limit (C)
maxTempC.description: Above this CPU temperature (the lower of the last two readings, so one spike does not count) the heat guard pauses heavy jobs

minBatteryPct.title: Minimum battery (%)
minBatteryPct.description: Below this, while discharging, the heat guard pauses heavy jobs

pauseOnBattery.title: Pause heavy jobs on battery
pauseOnBattery.description: The heat guard also holds heavy jobs whenever the laptop runs on battery, not only below the minimum

maxMemPct.title: Memory limit (%)
maxMemPct.description: The heat guard also holds heavy jobs while memory use is above this; 0 turns it off

heavyPattern.title: Heavy command pattern
heavyPattern.description: Regular expression for the Bash commands the heat guard treats as heavy, tested against the first words of each command in a line (after wrappers such as rtk, nice or npx), never its arguments; empty uses the built-in list

commandPrefix.title: Command prefix to track
commandPrefix.description: Bash commands are scored for starting with this word (for example rtk); empty turns the compliance meter off

threads.title: CPU threads
threads.description: Used to scale the load gauge; 0 detects it from the machine
